summary: After teaching something, a trainer asks a question built so the newcomers can show they were listening.
realLife: In orientation lectures, questions about what was just taught are worded so the expected answer displays knowledge, and the group answers back in short turns.
sources: Mikkola, Finding out what new employees know (conversation analysis of recorded orientation lectures), Työelämän tutkimus: https://journal.fi/tyoelamantutkimus/article/download/87105/46030/133414
inGame: the person's job record (employer, position, workplace) and the new-coworker event carry who and where; the speaker's habit is a line choice by trait; needs: a recorded orientation or training session

turns.summary: When no one answers, the trainer repeats the point and answers it themself.
turns.writesBack: a mood note that the room was stiff

turns.summary: One eager newcomer answers every time and others stay back.
pulledBy: a trainer who calls on volunteers
turns.writesBack: a tie between the eager newcomer and trainer; others stay unnoticed

turns.summary: The trainer lets the silence sit, then names the answer kindly.
turns.writesBack: a small trust bump from the quieter newcomers
